newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Government, sugar growers to build big new Zimbabwe dam.
newsitem.headline: Government, sugar growers to build big new Zimbabwe dam.

text.p: Zimbabwe's government has signed a joint venture deal with two major sugar cane growers to build the southern African country's biggest inland water body.
Land and Water Resources Minister Kumbirai Kangai told reporters the Tokwe-Mukosi dam would be constructed at a cost of over Z$390 million.
Triangle Ltd and Hippo Valley Estates would shoulder 60 percent of the total cost with the goverment putting in the remaining portion.

"We as a ministry have embraced this policy (of joint ventures with companies) with open arms as it allows us some latitude of independence as we do not have to rely on the fiscus and capital budget to develop our dams," Kangai said.

The new dam, with a capacity of over 1,700 billion cubic metres, is set to benefit sugar cane farmers in the drought-prone Masvingo province, where the crop was damaged during a drought in 1992 which saw Lake Mutirikwi, currently the country's largest inland reservoir, dry up.
